ALASKA IN WINTER

Fairbanks | Six days of winter and northern lights

A car-free Fairbanks base for dog sledding, hot springs, a city tour and heated aurora lodges. Leave the final night open so the trip does not mean staying out late every night.

Six-day overviewClothing and packingVisitor resources

This is a planning route, not a record of a completed trip. Tour times are local to Alaska. Follow your operator’s pickup notice for exact times, stops and drop-off.

DAY 01

Arrive in Fairbanks

ArrivalAirport and hotel shuttle

For a late flight, eat before landing. Check your lodging’s airport shuttle procedure and call for pickup after collecting bags.

DAY 02

Dog sledding, reindeer and aurora lodge

9:30 a.m.–5:45 p.m.Dog sledding and reindeer

Borealis Basecamp | Day trip

  1. Ready at 9:15 a.m.

    Pickup is typically 9:30–10:00 a.m. Group assignments determine the order of the forest dog-sled ride and the reindeer encounter.

  2. Lunch at Latitude 65

    This option lists a US$20 lunch voucher per person. Pay any difference and check that your chosen ticket includes it.

  3. Return around 5:15–5:45 p.m.

    Estimated camp departure is 4:30–5:00 p.m.; driving conditions and drop-off order affect the return.

What to wear Moisture-wicking base layer, fleece, windproof jacket, snow pants, wool socks and insulated grippy boots. Bring mittens, a hat, a neck gaiter and spare gloves. Check what winter gear the ticket includes.

Evening–2:30 a.m. next dayAurora Borealis Lodge

Have dinner first. A typical hotel pickup window is 9:30–10:05 p.m.; confirm yours with the operator. Return around 2:30 a.m. the next morning.

What to wear Wear a removable middle layer, warm coat and grippy footwear. Bring a parks passport or spare paper. Add thick gloves, a neck gaiter and hand warmers for aurora stops.

DAY 03

Chena Hot Springs and aurora

DaytimeRest and buy supplies

Leave the morning open after the late return. Buy food or water before the afternoon tour.

4:00 p.m.–2:00 a.m. next dayChena Hot Springs and aurora

Alaska Wild Lights | Afternoon to early morning

  1. 4:00–4:30 p.m.

    Hotel pickup. Approximate resort arrival is 5:30 p.m.; the listed package includes the ice museum.

  2. 7:00–9:00 p.m.

    Dinner is at your own expense. Bring a snack if helpful.

  3. 9:00–11:30 p.m.

    Hot springs and free time. Pool access is included in this option. Warm up indoors if needed.

  4. About 2:00 a.m. next day

    The operator adjusts roadside aurora stops according to clouds, road conditions and aurora activity.

What to wear Wear winter layers and pack a swimsuit, towel, grippy sandals, dry socks and a wet bag. Bring two quarters per locker; towel rental is extra.

DAY 04

Fairbanks sights and aurora glass house

1:00–6:30 p.m.Fairbanks Heritage Tour

Example afternoon departure: 1:00–about 6:30 p.m.

  1. Morris Thompson Visitor Center

    Start at the Public Lands Information Center for a National Parks passport stamp, then visit the cultural and nature exhibits. If you have seen the northern lights, ask the tourism desk about a certificate.

  2. Museum of the North

    Explore Alaska landscapes, wildlife and Alaska Native culture indoors. Check the admission details on your ticket.

  3. Trans-Alaska Pipeline

    A short outdoor stop for photos and a look at the aboveground pipeline.

  4. Santa Claus House in North Pole

    Browse the holiday shop and take photos; a Santa appearance is not guaranteed. Stop order may change seasonally.

What to wear Wear a removable middle layer, warm coat and grippy footwear. Bring a parks passport or spare paper. Add thick gloves, a neck gaiter and hand warmers for aurora stops.

9:30 p.m.–2:30 a.m. next dayCleary Summit aurora glass house

A heated cabin high on Cleary Summit, away from city lights. Floor-to-ceiling windows offer a 270° panorama. Wait inside with hot cocoa, coffee and snacks, then step outdoors for photos if the aurora appears. The tour offers aurora portraits when conditions allow; sightings are not guaranteed.

Have dinner in town first. This five-hour tour includes transport on the pickup option. A typical pickup window is 9:00–9:40 p.m.; check the operator text, and allow for a variable return.

What to wear Wear a removable middle layer, warm coat and grippy footwear. Bring a parks passport or spare paper. Add thick gloves, a neck gaiter and hand warmers for aurora stops.

DAY 05

Rest day or Thanksgiving

Daytime and eveningHoliday lunch and rest

Check holiday restaurant hours and reserve lunch if needed. Leave the evening open and ask your hotel about an aurora wake-up call. If clouds settle in, get a good night’s sleep.

DAY 06

Checkout and departure

Before departureHotel checkout and airport shuttle

Arrange your airport shuttle the night before. For holiday departures from FAI, arrive at least two hours early and allow extra time as needed.
